doc.title: Al Gafa interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 2, 2023

title: Current performing: trio, community concert and Zinc Bar
summary: He now plays with Alex Leonard and Jay Leonhart, drew a full house at his community, and played the Zinc Bar.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: You currently have opportunities to get out and perform?

I work every once in a while. I’m working with a trio, a piano player by the name of Alex Leonard, he sings and plays piano, he does both of them well — and Jay Leonhart is the bass player. So we just did a concert over here where I live, it was last week. It was the 27th of April. Normally the capacity is around 110, and they had to shut it down at 150 because they had a waiting list that could have reached 170. And it has to do with me, © Fillius Jazz Archive -18-

because in this community I’m a really good tennis player and there’s like 90 families in here that play tennis, and everybody in that community knows me because I’m a good tennis player. They showed up. There’s an arts group that would show up anyway whether I was here or not, and you know the word got around that they couldn’t handle the volume. But so yes I do get out and play and it’s usually with these three guys but every once in a while — oh I did a job at a club called the Zinc Bar in Manhattan. It was part of this guitar masters series. I did it with Jay and a piano player by the name of Ted Rosenthal. Excellent players both of them and I had to do two one-hour sets and both sets were sold out. And that’s a nice feeling, to go in and have that. I didn’t think I was that popular, I would have asked for more money.
